cell.label: Assess severity: <10% diaper area affected, faint to mild pink color, few or no satellite lesions, no ulceration, child is not distressed?

Mild diaper dermatitis Leave skin exposed as much as possible, frequent diaper changes, use fragrance-free, alcohol-free wipes or water to clean and avoid soaps or perfumed products, and apply a barrier paste (zinc oxide) at each diaper change.

Moderate/severe diaper dermatitis Treatment for mild diaper dermatitis, plus: (1) topical antifungal preparation (nystatin cream BID-TID), (2) topical corticosteroid (1% hydrocortisone cream BID), and (3) consider mupirocin or eosin.
Confirms diagnosis, minimize recurrence by continuing treatment for mild diaper dermatitis.
Ensure adequate treatment of opportunistic fungal infection; consider underlying skin disorder, such as eczema; consider alternate diagnoses.

footnotes.footnote: For moderate-severe dermatitis, opportunistic infection with Candida is likely. Although unsupported by evidence, a blend of Aquaphor ointment (4 parts), stomahesive paste (2 parts), and nystatin cream (1 part) compounded by a pharmacist as "butt paste"; is often prescribed, with anecdotal benefits.
Adapted from National Health Service (NHS). Management of nappy rash in children. Available at https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/pregnancy-and-baby/nappy-rash/.
